content.text:
Staygreen has two plans, Free and Builder, defined in one table in `src/lib/plans.ts:73-110`. A Builder workspace is one whose Clerk session holds the `scale_builder` feature; any other result, including an error reading Clerk, counts as Free (`src/lib/plans.ts:145-161`). Most count limits are enforced in Postgres functions, which receive the numbers from the app on every call. Two Free limits (MCP monitors and 10-minute MCP checks) are listed but nothing enforces them yet.

## The limits

| Limit | Free | Builder |
|---|---|---|
| Apps | 1 | 10 |
| Status pages | 1 | 10 |
| Monitors (the auto-added SSL monitor is not counted) | 50 | 100 |
| Monitors per host (SSL monitors not counted) | 5 | "fair use", which means the monitor limit |
| HTTP / TCP check interval | 3 min | 1 min |
| Stripe poll interval | 10 min | 5 min |
| Stripe monitors | 1 | 3 |
| Supabase monitors | 1 | "cap", which means the monitor limit |
| MCP monitors / MCP check interval | 2 / 10 min | cap / 5 min |
| Heartbeat monitors | 5 | 50 |
| Assertions per HTTP monitor | 3 | 10 |
| Assertions per heartbeat | 1 | 5 |
| Probe locations | Toronto, San Francisco | adds Frankfurt |
| History | 30 days | 1 year |
| API / MCP calls per minute | 30 | 120 |

All rows come from `src/lib/plans.ts:73-110`.

- **Feature switches.** Each of these is its own Clerk feature, all included in Builder: `white_label`, `private_pages`, `subscribers`, `alert_rules`, `history_1y`, `notify_teammates` (`src/lib/plans.ts:11-19,166-174`).
- **Demo plan.** There is also a private owner-only demo plan, `scale_demo`: Builder plus 100 apps, 1000 monitors, 500 heartbeats and 100 status pages (`src/lib/plans.ts:112-117`).
- **Self-hosted.** `SELF_HOSTED_PLAN=builder` gives every workspace Builder's normal limits, never the demo counts (`src/lib/self-hosted-plan.ts:5-10`, `src/lib/session.ts:32`). The app refuses to start with it on Staygreen's own hosted domains (`src/lib/env-schema.ts:130-134`).

## Where each limit is enforced

The app reads the session's limits and passes them as arguments to Postgres functions. The functions lock the workspace row, count, and refuse (`src/lib/plans.ts:6-7`). If a limit argument is missing they raise `limits_required`, so a call can't skip the check. Refusals become readable messages in `src/lib/db-errors.ts:56-67`.

**Apps** → `create_app` counts the workspace's apps and raises `app_limit` (`supabase/migrations/20261022124400_apps_limit_and_logo.sql:55-68`). It's called from `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:109-115`. A workspace already over the limit keeps its apps; only the next one is refused (`:63-64`).

**Status pages** → `create_status_page` raises `page_limit` (`supabase/migrations/20261021210216_phase1_dashboard.sql:410-422`), called from `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:827-834`.

**HTTP, TCP, SSL, DNS and heartbeat monitors** → `create_monitor`, latest version in `supabase/migrations/20261022040000_heartbeat_url_sealed.sql:29-118`, called from `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:232-253`:
- Monitor count: `monitor_limit`, counting `not auto` rows (`:82-85`).
- Heartbeat count: `heartbeat_limit` (`:87-92`).
- Assertions: `assertion_limit`, using the heartbeat or HTTP limit depending on type (`:94-99`).
- Interval:
  - HTTP and TCP must be at least the plan minimum.
  - DNS must be at least 600 s.
  - SSL is fixed at 21600 s.
  - All three raise `interval_not_allowed` (`:101-105`).
- Per host: `host_limit`, SSL excluded (`:107-113`).

**Editing a monitor** → `update_monitor` repeats the assertion, interval and per-host checks but not the count (`supabase/migrations/20261022081211_monitor_edit_closes_incident.sql:39-82`; caller `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:346-365`).

**Stripe and Supabase monitors** → `save_service_monitor`, called from `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:308-316`. On create it checks:
- total monitors (`monitor_limit`);
- monitors of that type (`service_monitor_limit`), using `stripeAccounts`, or for Supabase the cap turned into the monitor limit;
- monitors per host.

The interval is limited to fixed values: 60 or 180 s for Supabase, 300 or 600 s for Stripe (`supabase/migrations/20261023100000_service_monitors.sql:15-60`).

**Agent / REST / MCP writes** → `src/lib/agent-service.ts:197` sends the same limits as JSON. `agent_write` refuses if any limit is missing (`supabase/migrations/20261023150000_agent_surface.sql:130-131`), and `agent_create_monitor` calls the same `create_monitor` / `save_service_monitor` (`:91-118`).

**Demo clone** passes app, page, monitor, assertion, per-host and interval limits to `clone_demo_page` (`src/app/(app)/app/clone/[slug]/actions.ts:44-46`, `supabase/migrations/20261028220000_demo_clone_branding.sql:45-58`).

**Custom domain verification** passes the monitor and per-host limits to `verify_page_domain` (`src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:982-985`, `supabase/migrations/20261023140000_status_edge.sql:175-187`).

**API rate** → `src/lib/agent-auth.ts:130` charges a per-workspace budget of `apiPerMin`. `agent_budget` uses a one-minute window and rejects any limit above 120 (`supabase/migrations/20261023150000_agent_surface.sql:73-87`). Separately, a workspace may hold at most 100 unrevoked API tokens on any plan (`:66`).

**Locations** are enforced by the probes, not the app:
- A Frankfurt probe refuses to start without `PROBE_BUILDER_ONLY=true` (`probe/env.ts:18`).
- `eligible` drops builder-only probes for non-Builder monitors (`probe/schedule.ts:46-47`).
- Probes learn which workspaces are Builder from `probe_builder_workspaces` (`probe/store.ts:209-220`). That reads the `plan` column, which `syncWorkspacePlan` copies from the session (`src/lib/workspace-plan.ts:20`).

**History** → the agent API caps history windows at 30 or 365 days by `history_1y` (`src/lib/agent-service.ts:52,276`; contract text at `src/lib/agent-contract.ts:28`). Old data is never deleted: the docs say retention cleanup isn't built (`docs/architecture.md:50`), and I found no deletion job in the migrations.

**Feature switches** are checked in server actions and passed into SQL:
- `white_label` and `private_pages`: `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:874-875,894-895`.
- `notify_teammates`: `src/app/(app)/app/alerts/actions.ts:122,139`.
- `alert_rules`: `src/app/(app)/app/alerts/actions.ts:317,322`.
- `subscribers`: no server code checks it. The billing screen marks email subscribers as coming soon (`src/app/(app)/app/billing/BillingScreen.tsx:115`).

## Gaps and quirks

- **MCP limits are listed but not enforced.** `create_monitor` only accepts `http`, `ssl`, `dns`, `tcp` and `heartbeat` (`supabase/migrations/20261022040000_heartbeat_url_sealed.sql:70-74`). The plan table marks MCP as "soon" (`src/components/PlanTable.tsx:44`). `mcpMonitors` and `mcpIntervalMin` are only displayed.
- **Upgrading speeds monitors up; downgrading doesn't slow them.**

The app reads the session's limits and passes them as arguments to Postgres functions. The functions lock the workspace row, count, and refuse (`src/lib/plans.ts:6-7`). If a limit argument is missing they raise `limits_required`, so a call can't skip the check. Refusals become readable messages in `src/lib/db-errors.ts:56-67`.

**Apps** → `create_app` counts the workspace's apps and raises `app_limit` (`supabase/migrations/20261022124400_apps_limit_and_logo.sql:55-68`). It's called from `src/app/(app)/app/actions.ts:109-115`. A workspace already over the limit keeps its apps; only the next one is refused (`:63-64`).
